questions.question: What is encapsulation in Ruby?
questions.title: Encapsulation in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Encapsulation = bundle state with the methods that act on it, and hide internals from outside. In Ruby: instance variables (@x) are ALWAYS private — outsiders can't read or set them directly. You expose state via methods (attr_reader :name, a custom balance method) and control mutation (def balance=(v); raise if v < 0; @balance = v; end). Private methods (private keyword; def private_m; end) can only be called without a receiver (self.private_m raises; just private_m works) — they're internal helpers. Protected (protected) can be called by other instances of the same class. Encapsulation keeps invariants: a BankAccount's @balance is only changed through deposit/withdraw, which can enforce rules. Use attr_reader over attr_accessor; make helpers private; expose a small public API. This decouples internals from users.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know @vars are always private, private methods need no receiver, and you expose state via methods.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Trying self.private_m (raises — private methods take no receiver), or using attr_accessor when attr_reader would do.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Encapsulation = bundle state + methods, hide internals. @vars always private. private = no receiver; protected = same class. Expose via attr_reader.

sections.title: Encapsulation
sections.content:
```ruby
class BankAccount
  def initialize(owner); @owner = owner; @balance = 0; end

  # PUBLIC API: expose state via methods
  attr_reader :owner, :balance

  # Controlled mutation (enforces an INVARIANT)
  def deposit(amount)
    raise 'must be positive' if amount <= 0
    @balance += amount
  end
  def withdraw(amount)
    raise 'insufficient' if amount > @balance
    @balance -= amount
  end

  private                 # everything below is private
  def fee; 1; end         # internal helper (no receiver)
  def apply_fee; @balance -= fee; end
end

acct = BankAccount.new('Ada')
acct.owner            # 'Ada'   (public getter)
acct.balance          # 0      (public getter)
acct.deposit(100)     # controlled mutation
acct.withdraw(30)
acct.balance          # 70

# @balance is PRIVATE — can't read/write directly:
# acct.balance = -5    # NoMethodError (no setter) — invariant protected
# acct.@balance        # syntax error

# Private methods: called WITHOUT a receiver:
# acct.fee             # NoMethodError (private, needs receiver)
# self.fee             # NoMethodError (private can't take a receiver)
fee                   # works only INSIDE the class (no receiver)

# Protected: callable by other instances of the same class
class Pair
  protected
  def secret; 42; end
  def other_secret(p); p.secret; end   # ok: same class
end
```
